# Home Assistant integration for UniFi Drive / UNAS v0.9.0b1

**Beta 1: opt-in testing, not a stable release.** This prerelease combines storage
diagnostics and monitoring improvements with the previously unreleased 0.9.0
runtime-hardening work. The stable release channel remains unchanged.

Existing `0.8.0+` installations update in place: no new domain change, reinstall
or entity migration is required. Back up Home Assistant before trying the beta.

## New In This Beta

- Updates the current HA validation baseline to stable `2026.11.0` with its
  matching official Core test helpers and Python `3.14`. Setup/unload follow
  the modern success/exception contract while retaining older HA support.
- Updates CodeQL to `4.39.3`, Checkout to `7.0.1`, Setup Python to `7.1.0`,
  Release Action to `3.0.4`, Hassfest's pinned revision and Ruff to `0.17.4`.
- API-key metadata fallbacks improve device firmware/Drive version, CPU
  temperature and uptime readings. Uptime stays at its last sample when offline.
- Optional SSD-cache and SMART diagnostics expose remaining life and sector-error
  counts only when reported. Drive diagnostics are disabled by default; enabling
  them adds Recorder history, so enable only the readings you need.
- RAID-group progress and scrubbing metadata supplement pool maintenance readings
  without treating SSD-cache progress as data-pool maintenance.
- Independent metadata reads run concurrently with short timeouts. Static system
  metadata is cached for up to ten minutes and invalidated on connection failures
  or explicit refreshes; live storage/control readings keep their existing cadence.
- Multi-pool tests cover four, seven and eight data disks, two cache SSDs,
  reordered payloads, stable IDs, offline recovery and diagnostics redaction.
- A hardware report form and evidence matrix make unverified models and fields
  explicit. **UNAS Pro, Pro4 and Pro8 are not yet confirmed on real hardware.**

## Included Reliability Work

- Fixes reauthentication and reconfiguration on Home Assistant `2024.8.0`, with
  tests that reject a different device without changing existing credentials.
- Caps decompressed HTTP response bodies at 8 MiB across monitoring, login,
  errors and actions. Oversized responses fail with a privacy-safe error rather
  than accumulating an unrestricted response body.
- Adds actual HA flow-manager tests for setup retry/abort, options validation,
  identity preservation, reloads and repair recovery.
- Adds real SQLite Recorder tests for unchanged polling, throughput exclusions,
  cached offline data and snapshot-control attribute deduplication.
- Measures repeated setup/unload and continuous polling with changing snapshot
  targets. Inventory caches drop inactive targets; existing entity groups remain
  available for automations and missing-target handling.
- Expands strict typing to every integration module and checks selected HA
  interfaces against real imported types.
- Adds scheduled synthetic resource checks and verifies published release tags,
  notes and installation ZIPs against the release source.

## Compatibility And Scope

The tested HA baselines are `2024.8.0` / Python `3.12` and stable `2026.11.0` /
Python `3.14` (HA requires at least `3.14.2`). HA `2026.11` is not a new minimum
requirement. Live Marketplace lifecycle validation remains separate follow-up work.

The full local suite passes on each baseline, with coverage above 95%.
Resource measurements are synthetic regression tests, not a new live NAS soak or
a guarantee of constant RAM with unlimited new snapshot target identities.
Global Recorder settings, statistics retention and purge behavior are unchanged.

Cached offline readings and Wake-on-LAN are preserved. Local snapshot, fan,
backup and update controls remain experimental and firmware/permission dependent.
No destructive snapshot actions are added. Quality Scale gaps remain documented;
this is not an official Platinum certification.

## Trying The Beta

In HACS, enable prerelease versions in the repository's version selection and
select **v0.9.0b1**, then restart Home Assistant. The beta is not promoted to the
stable Marketplace/HACS update channel. Marketplace availability and version
selection depend on the installed HA/catalog version.

Check device versions, pool/disk assignment and any cache readings against the
NAS UI. Keep experimental controls disabled unless you specifically intend to
test them. Report missing, duplicate or incorrect readings with reviewed HA
diagnostics, never raw API payloads or private identifiers. See the
[hardware reporting guide](https://github.com/memphi2/ha-unifi-drive/blob/v0.9.0b1/docs/hardware_validation.md).

To leave the beta, select the latest stable version in HACS and restart Home
Assistant. Beta-only entities may no longer be provided. Restore your pre-beta
backup if needed; no config-entry migration is introduced by this beta.

## Updating Existing Installations

For integration versions `0.8.0` and newer, back up Home Assistant, install the
offered update and complete any requested restart. Keep the existing integration
entry, device and entities. Moving from HACS to Marketplace does not require a
reinstall.

**Versions before `0.8.0` require removal and reinstallation** because the old
`unifi_drive` domain was replaced by `unifi_unas`. This is the earlier breaking
change, not a new migration introduced in `0.9.0b1`:

1. Back up Home Assistant and note affected automation/dashboard references.
2. Remove the old integration entries under `Settings` -> `Devices & services`.
3. Uninstall the downloaded integration through HACS or Marketplace to remove its
   managed files. Deleting only a device or config entry does not remove the code.
4. For manual installations, or if the old folder remains after uninstalling,
   remove only `/config/custom_components/unifi_drive/`. Do not edit `.storage`.
5. Restart Home Assistant, install the current integration through the appropriate
   installation method, then add **UniFi Drive / UNAS** again.
6. Check affected automations and dashboards. Do not retain both domains for the
   same NAS.

See the [installation guide](https://github.com/memphi2/ha-unifi-drive/blob/v0.9.0b1/docs/installation.md)
for Marketplace, HACS and manual procedures.
